solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Light rain: Jack sheltering in hollow that's welcoming

indicators.note: something sheltering in a place sits inside it, so the first words go within the hollow

blocks.note: to spit is to rain very lightly
a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)

explanation.surface: A drizzly day in which a sailor shelters in a dip in the ground, finding it welcoming.
explanation.walkthrough: Light rain looks like part of a weather report, but spit is a verb for drizzling; jack is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospitable host is friendly and generous to guests, which is what welcoming describes.

clue.text: After trip, stop game

indicators.note: the second word is placed after the first, giving the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a hop is a short trip
to scotch a plan is to stop it

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt a game after a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch as a verb means to put an end to something, as in scotching a rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground pastime of hopping between chalked squares.

clue.text: Saucy thing beginning to strip — a boy doing otherwise?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: the opposite of stripping is putting clothes on

explanation.surface: A racy striptease scene where a young man does the reverse and puts his clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip is both the source of S and the cue: a boy doing the opposite of stripping is A LAD DRESSING.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad dressing is a sauce poured over leaves, so it is literally a thing made of sauce.

clue.text: Island, a short distance

blocks.note: first meaning: in Scotland and Ireland an ... is a small island
second meaning: an imperial unit of length, or any small amount of space

explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish sense, as in Inchcolm, is the one solvers outside Scotland may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small Scottish or Irish islet and a tiny unit of length, twelfth of a foot.

clue.text: Sat on Titanic so agitated, prepare for a battle!

indicators.note: agitated things are shaken up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Passengers sitting aboard the doomed liner grow panicky, as if bracing for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Action stations is the naval command for crews to take their posts ready for combat.

clue.text: In Nepal, a meteor hit

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the country, the article and the start of the space rock

explanation.surface: A shooting star crashing to earth in the Himalayan kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam someone is an informal verb for striking or thrashing them hard.

clue.text: Ignorant group is taken in by hacker

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held within it

blocks.note: a nonet is a group of nine

explanation.surface: A gang has been infiltrated by a computer intruder.
explanation.walkthrough: Hacker suggests computers, but here it is someone chopping with an axe; a nonet is a group of nine musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Being none the wiser means knowing no more than before, so still uninformed about something.

clue.text: Original ode's first up for poet

indicators.note: the first of a word is just its opening letter
in a down entry, going up means the letters read from the bottom

explanation.surface: The opening of a fresh poem is lifted up as a tribute to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilfred Owen was the English First World War poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred Owen wrote Dulce et Decorum Est and other famous war verse, so he is a poet.

clue.text: One seeing English tree, it overlooking cape

indicators.note: in a down entry, a part overlooking another sits above it

blocks.note: a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbours along the coast

explanation.surface: Someone describes an English tree standing above a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness appears in many British coastal place names, such as Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is a person who saw an event happen with their own eyes.

clue.text: Party bringing leaders of neighbouring nations into prominence

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the words that follow
the selected letters are put inside the next word

blocks.note: height is prominence, a rise above the surroundings

explanation.surface: A political party drawing border states into the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen night is the British name for a bride's pre-wedding party with her female friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a celebration held for a woman shortly before her wedding, so a kind of gathering.

clue.text: Extraordinary female made up new word where Arabic spoken

indicators.note: made up means invented or composed, so these letters are assembled afresh

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A remarkable woman coins a fresh term in an Arab land.
explanation.walkthrough: Wonder Woman is the DC comics superheroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonder Woman is a superpowered comic-book heroine, and the phrase also describes any exceptionally capable woman.

clue.text: Protected pigs ultimately led there to be slaughtered

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it
slaughtered things are butchered, so these letters are cut up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Pigs being herded to the abattoir, hardly a protected existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered means shielded from harm or hardship, kept out of danger's way.

clue.text: Little jumper, fine top

blocks.note: a roo is a kangaroo, small in name if not in leap
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Shopping for a small sweater and a nice top to go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is the British word for a sweater, which is the surface sense; here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The roof is the uppermost covering of a building, its top.

clue.text: Together in neatly arranged houses

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it inside

blocks.note: hair that is combed is neatly arranged

explanation.surface: Homes laid out in tidy rows side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: In is the inner piece rather than a link word, and houses is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are combined are joined into one, so acting jointly or as a unit.

clue.text: Animal has tail at first, one to cut back

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it
going back means the whole string is read from right to left

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A creature's tail is the first thing someone wants to trim.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a dark-furred carnivorous mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Source of wealth around old church of a distant epoch

indicators.note: around means wrapped about the following letters

blocks.note: a mine of gold or gems is a source of riches
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Riches gathered around an ancient church from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival, as in Miocene fossils.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miocene is a geological period roughly 23 to 5 million years ago, used as an adjective for things from it.

clue.text: Emperor carrying on with unknown character — that's anything but love?

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it within

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler persisting with a mysterious figure, hardly a love story.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring, so anything but love is any score other than nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonzero describes any quantity other than nought, and love is the tennis term for a nil score.

clue.text: Mock a noted conclusion

blocks.note: cod as an adjective means fake or mock, as in cod philosophy

explanation.surface: Jeering at a famous person's final remark.
explanation.walkthrough: Noted looks like famous, but it means written in musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a piece of music, its ending in written notes.

clue.text: Discussion involving Tory — amazing

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories
fab is slang for fabulous or amazing

explanation.surface: A wonderful debate featuring a Conservative politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab is an informal chat or conference, short for confabulation.

clue.text: Lit up at dinnertime, darling goes in to eat

indicators.note: goes in means is placed inside the following word

blocks.note: lamb is an affectionate term for a darling
to feed is to eat, as animals do

explanation.surface: A beloved arrives for dinner to eat, everyone in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Lit up suggests drunk or illuminated; here food is set alight with spirits at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambéed food has brandy poured over it and is set on fire, so it is lit up during a meal.

clue.text: Attentive chap from East Timor?

blocks.note: Dili is the capital of East Timor
a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: Asking about a man who hails from a small south-east Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: a chap from the capital of East Timor might be a Dili gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent means careful and hard-working, giving close heed to a task.

clue.text: Identical daughter gets hold of bandage finally for wound

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it within
finally points to the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A twin girl clutches a dressing for an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound looks like an injury, matching bandage, but it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Twined is the past tense of twine, meaning twisted or coiled, just as wound is from wind.

clue.text: Inspired by rock, style of music to perform — that's for dropouts?

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so it goes inside the next word

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A rock band influencing a musical style for students who left college.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropouts suggests people who quit school; here they are things that literally drop out through a hatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor is a hinged opening in a floor or stage through which people or things fall.

clue.text: Weariest when travelling, in a kind of way

indicators.note: letters that travel move about and end up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Feeling most tired on a journey, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were is a phrase meaning so to speak, softening an expression to a sort of manner.

clue.text: Now partner has ruined everything, after happening to cause upset

annotation.answer: THROW A SPANNER IN THE WORKS

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order
the second part is placed after the first, giving the order

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram
the works means everything, the lot

explanation.surface: A partner has wrecked it all, and only after the event comes the fallout.
explanation.walkthrough: To throw a spanner in the works is the British idiom; Americans say a monkey wrench.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sabotage a plan or disrupt a smooth process, so to bring about trouble.

clue.text: Girl has put short stockings on — hallelujah!

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter
with one part put on the other, the two are set side by side

explanation.surface: A young woman has pulled on her tights, praise be!
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a cry of praise or adoration to God, as hallelujah also is.

clue.text: Friend a nuisance in European city

blocks.note: bud is American slang for a pal

explanation.surface: A pal turns out to be irritating on a trip to a continental capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital of Hungary, on the Danube.

clue.text: In a fine spray deodorant initially contained

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it
contained means held inside the preceding phrase

blocks.note: a mist is a fine spray of droplets

explanation.surface: An aerosol deodorant releases its contents as a fine spray.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like a link word at the start, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst is a preposition meaning surrounded by or in the middle of, which in can also express.

clue.text: Mean knock?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cruel blow, or an unkind remark
setter's reading: the average score of a cricketer's innings, a knock being an innings

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a knock is an innings and the mean is an average, so a batsman's typical score is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A batting average is a cricketer's total runs divided by dismissals, the arithmetic mean of each innings.

clue.text: Thickness not diminished, roughly about right

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, so the letters are only loosely kept in order
about means placed around the following letter

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A dimension that has not been reduced, approximately correct.
explanation.definitionFit: After length and breadth, depth or thickness is the third measurable direction of a solid object.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical governors the chief enemy in conclusion

indicators.note: in conclusion points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: arch means principal, as in arch-rival

explanation.surface: Church rulers regard the leading adversary as finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A thearchy is rule by a god or a body of divine or priestly rulers, a governing hierarchy of the church.

clue.text: English town succeeded before the French city

indicators.note: before places the first parts ahead of the next ones

blocks.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
Lens is a city in northern France

explanation.surface: An English town did well ahead of a French city in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: St Helens is a town in Merseyside, known for its rugby league club.
explanation.definitionFit: St Helens is a town in north-west England between Liverpool and Wigan.

clue.text: Pernicious lady about to steal fella's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter
about means wrapped around what follows

blocks.note: to nab is to steal or snatch

explanation.surface: A wicked woman plans to break a man's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame is a title for a lady, and the heart of fella is one of its two middle Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnable means deserving condemnation, hateful, so harmful and wicked like something pernicious.

clue.text: Singer ending in club like so, for enjoyable party

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A vocalist finishing in a nightclub, enjoying the party scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Like is AS and so is taken as written; pro is Latin for for.
explanation.definitionFit: A basso profundo is a singer with an exceptionally deep bass voice.

clue.text: Match fit, perhaps, though no start in store

indicators.note: with no start, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a boxing match is a bout
a fit of pique is a burst of resentment; perhaps flags the example

explanation.surface: An athlete is fit for the game but not picked to start, so it stays in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small fashionable shop, a kind of store.

clue.text: Interesting it's coming together

blocks.note: second meaning: meshing, as gears do, or meeting in battle

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as a phrase: gears that are coming together are said to be engaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means appealing and attention-holding, and also describes parts meshing or opponents meeting in combat.

clue.text: Essay on wheat, book totally factual

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part on another sits above it

blocks.note: an essay is an attempt, as is a go
spelt is an ancient variety of wheat
the Book of Ruth in the Bible

explanation.surface: A paper written on cereal crops in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Essay looks like a piece of writing, but it means a try.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel truth is something completely true, as unquestionable as scripture.

clue.text: Turning scarlet, the sour dessert

indicators.note: turning means the letters are spun round into another order

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A pudding that has gone off, going red and tasting acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte russe is a cold pudding of Bavarian cream set in a mould lined with sponge fingers.

clue.text: Curiosity — artist needs it to read between the lines?

indicators.note: to read between two things puts it in the gap inside them

explanation.surface: A painter must understand subtle hidden meaning in a work.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading between the lines suggests spotting implied meaning; here IT literally goes between R and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something uncommon and prized, a curiosity worth seeing.

clue.text: Hot stuff, with nothing in court case being vulgar

indicators.note: in places one item inside the next

blocks.note: a trial is a legal case in court

explanation.surface: A sexy celebrity with no court case to answer behaving coarsely.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot stuff suggests an attractive person; here it is lava.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavatorial humour is crude toilet humour, so the word describes coarse and smutty talk.

clue.text: About to marry deadwood

blocks.note: to fuse is to join or unite

explanation.surface: A couple are about to wed, but one is dead weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is waste matter, rubbish to be thrown out, as useless deadwood is.

clue.text: Details I infer scattered around page on book

indicators.note: scattered letters are thrown about and land in another order
around means wrapped about the next letter
in a down entry, one part on another sits above it

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A reader draws conclusions from pages spread across a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine print is the small-type particulars of a contract, the details easily missed.

clue.text: Stairs including an opening

indicators.note: including means holding the next word inside

explanation.surface: A staircase leads up to a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a small window, often semicircular, over a door, an opening that lets in light.

clue.text: Criminal comedian admitting beaten, finally

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in
finally points to the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A comic owns up at last to having been defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of an organised criminal gang.

clue.text: Anxious over cracks in heater returning

indicators.note: cracks means breaks up, so the word before it is rearranged
in places the jumbled letters inside the following word
returning means the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Worrying about splits appearing in the radiator coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Cracks looks like a noun but is a verb: it breaks up the word over before that goes inside the reversed heater.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous means apprehensive and worried, so uneasy about what may happen.

clue.text: Distract team with song

explanation.surface: Putting the players off their game by singing at them.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack someone is to divert their attention away from the main issue.

clue.text: A bit of water and a second, neither quite finding sea

indicators.note: not quite complete means both words lose their last letters

blocks.note: a drip is a small drop of water
a tick is a moment or second

explanation.surface: A tiny amount of water and a moment's wait, never quite reaching the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Both phrases lose their final letter: A DRI(P) and A TIC(K).
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is the arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans.

clue.text: Having saved little US cash, silly granddad, he wed nan, getting severely punished

indicators.note: having saved means holding something inside, kept safe
silly means foolish and disordered, so the letters that follow are muddled

blocks.note: a quarter is a 25-cent US coin, a small sum
taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A foolish grandfather married grandma after putting aside some American money, and paid harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram letters wrap around QUARTER, which sits before the final two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging, drawing and quartering was the old English execution for high treason, the harshest penalty possible.

clue.text: Quibble darling? Move well back!

indicators.note: back means the preceding words are read from right to left

blocks.note: a pet is a darling or favourite
a go is a move in a game

explanation.surface: An argument over a sweetheart who is told firmly to step away.
explanation.walkthrough: Move well looks like a phrase, but each word is separate before the pair is turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: To pettifog is to argue over trivial points, to quibble about petty details.

clue.text: State having twisted story, journalist going into it

indicators.note: a twisted word is turned round to read backwards
going into means being placed within

explanation.surface: A nation where a reporter has spun a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian country, a sovereign nation or state.

clue.text: Suspect image for recollection, provided in terrible case

indicators.note: read as re-collection, gathering the letters back the other way
in places the following word inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A police sketch of a suspect drawn from a witness's memory, set in a dreadful case.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal signal is weak, resting on recollection read as collecting again in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-fit is an electronic facial composite of a suspect built from a witness's memory.

clue.text: Dish — or pot?

blocks.note: first meaning: a fried mixture of chopped meat and potato
second meaning: cannabis, short for hashish

explanation.walkthrough: Dish and pot look like kitchenware; pot is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cooked dish of chopped leftovers and is also slang for the cannabis resin hashish.

clue.text: Sculptor's piece in pieces!

blocks.note: first meaning: a sculpture of head and shoulders

explanation.walkthrough: The two uses of piece pull in opposite directions: an artwork, then something smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a sculpted head and shoulders and an informal adjective for broken.

clue.text: Something more luxurious, cut

indicators.note: cut means the word is trimmed of its last letter

explanation.surface: A rather fancier item, chopped down.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an extra or advantage, something additional on top of what is expected.

clue.text: Equal measure in a tumbler originally containing reduced drink

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word before it
reduced means the word is cut short by its last letter
containing means holding the following within

explanation.surface: Pouring a fair share of a reduced spirit into a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: A and T enclose LIQUO(R).
explanation.definitionFit: An aliquot is a portion that divides a whole exactly, so one of several equal parts or measures.

clue.text: Mineral container one returned, awaiting delivery

indicators.note: returned means the preceding words are read backwards

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: A parcel of minerals in a box is sent back, still waiting for the courier.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery suggests the post; here it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: In utero means in the womb, describing a baby not yet born, so waiting to be delivered.

clue.text: A female with nothing up top?

definitions.text: A female with nothing up top?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up top means placed at the head above the rest

explanation.surface: A woman described as bald, or perhaps as empty-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: someone with nothing up top is brainless.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy stupid person, one with nothing much in the head.

clue.text: Finally abandoning south for north, then a southern US city

indicators.note: one letter is dropped and another put in its place

explanation.surface: Someone eventually leaves the South for the North, then a Southern city.
explanation.walkthrough: The S in AT LAST becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital of Georgia, in the American South.

clue.text: Drink in exciting bars, say?

blocks.note: chocolate comes in bars; say marks the example

explanation.surface: Having a drink in some lively pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bars suggests pubs, matching drink, but here they are slabs of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate is a warm beverage made from cocoa and milk.

clue.text: Sweet wine no great shakes?

blocks.note: afters is British slang for dessert
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A dessert wine that is nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: No great shakes normally means mediocre; here it is a smaller tremor following an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftershock is a lesser tremor after the main quake, literally not a great shaking.
